newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - AlliedSignal To aquire Grimes.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - AlliedSignal To aquire Grimes.

text.p: AlliedSignal said it would buy Grimes Aerospace, a major aircraft lighting supplier, from an affiliate of investment firm Forstmann Little and Co. Terms were not disclosed. The acquisition is expected to be non-dilutive to AlliedSignal earnings in 1997 and should contribute to earnings in 1998. A full text of the company's press release follows.
Aerospace, World's Largest Supplier Of Aircraft Lighting Systems, From Forstmann Little

MORRIS TOWNSHIP, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--June 18, 1997--AlliedSignal Inc. announced today that it has agreed to acquire Grimes Aerospace, the world's leading supplier of aircraft lighting systems, from an affiliate of Forstmann Little & Co., a New York investment firm. Terms of the transaction, which is subject to regulatory review, were not announced.

Grimes Aerospace manufactures exterior and interior lighting systems, strobes, night vision imaging systems and power supplies. It also supplies aircraft engine systems, including valves and heat exchangers, and electronic systems, including flight warning computers, active matrix liquid crystal displays and windshield wiper systems. Customers include Boeing, Airbus, Pratt & Whitney, de Havilland, Sikorsky, Northrop Grumman, Gulfstream and Bell Helicopter, as well as most commercial airlines.

"Grimes Aerospace's world-leading aircraft lighting systems are an important addition to our aerospace product offerings, while the valves, heat exchangers and electronic systems will provide us with new product offerings in those industry segments," said Daniel P. Burnham, president of AlliedSignal Aerospace. Grimes Aerospace's shipset value ranges from $50,000 to $200,000 per commercial aircraft.

Grimes Aerospace's annual sales, currently approximately $230 million, are growing at a double-digit annual rate. About 70% of the company's business is commercial and 30% military; about 40% is original equipment and 60% aftermarket. "Grimes Aerospace's well managed distribution channels and customer support systems are an excellent fit with our growing aftermarket parts and repair and overhaul business," said Burnham.

AlliedSignal said that it expects the acquisition to be nondilutive in 1997 and to contribute to earnings beginning in 1998. Founded in 1933, Grimes Aerospace has 1,400 employees worldwide, with primary facilities and product support centers in Urbana, Ohio; Greenwood, South Carolina; Plymouth and Bristol, Connecticut; and Ocala, Florida.

AlliedSignal Aerospace is the world's leading supplier of aerospace equipment, with a broad product line that includes propulsion engines, auxiliary power units, power management systems, engine systems and accessories, environmental control systems, avionics, flight safety systems, wheels and brakes, as well as repair and overhaul services. It is a unit of AlliedSignal Inc., a $14 billion (sales) advanced technology and manufacturing company serving customers worldwide with aerospace and automotive products, chemicals, fibers, plastics and advanced materials.
